chapter: Wynn: New York and Chicago bands
title: Jimmie Noone's band at the Cabin Inn
summary: Wynn rejoined Noone after Henderson's band broke up, broadcasting on WBBM, and remembers Noone's love of food.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: He broke up the band in Boston. And he went with Benny. So I come back and joined Jimmy Noon again at another place down at 35th Street. The Platinum Lounge, maybe?
That's where I came from. 35th and State. It was the same spot that I'd worked in. Cabin Inn, they called it. Oh, yeah, sure.
It used to be in the 34th block.
Yeah. It was the Death Blocker movement.

Yeah. So I worked with Jimmy until that fall. We were on WBBM there, broadcasting. And it was, he had a big band there. It was a nice, happy relationship. Jimmy was one of another one of those grand leaders. He was one of the most remarkable fellows you ever want to work with.
Yeah, he was wonderful, too. Wonderful, wonderful fellow. I knew him fairly well. I heard him a few times.

And one thing stands out in my mind about him, his love for food. He loved to eat. Yep. And when he wasn't eating, he would like to talk about it. He would have just got up from dinner and come to work, and he's telling you what he had for dinner in my hands. He'd go into all details, whatever little thing he had. And he just got there, and we just hit in the first setting. He would call the waitress, have me a half a chicken right at intermission. We'd take an intermission about half an hour after we started, because we had to get ready for the broadcast. And he would be all ready to eat all over. He was terrific. Wonderful to work with. Never, never no hassle either way.
